# Sonda Red

Sonda Red is Kalin Daskalov's personal engineering lab for Kubernetes-native AI infrastructure, workload identity, inference systems, operators, and platform engineering.

This is not a company, vendor, product platform, or AI governance platform. Content and projects are by Kalin Daskalov unless otherwise noted.

## Canonical Site Sections

- Home: https://sonda.red/
- Notes archive: https://sonda.red/notes/
- About Kalin Daskalov: https://sonda.red/about/
- Kleym project documentation: https://kleym.sonda.red/
- Source namespace: https://github.com/sonda-red

## Main Topics

- Kubernetes-native AI infrastructure
- Intel Arc GPU homelab operations
- vLLM, llm-d, OpenWebUI, and inference routing
- Dynamic Resource Allocation for Kubernetes GPUs
- SPIFFE, SPIRE, workload identity, and controller-based registration
- Kubernetes operators and controller-runtime
- FluxCD, GitOps, observability, and platform engineering

## Selected Notes

- https://sonda.red/notes/09-xpumanager/ - Replacing a custom Intel XPU Manager deployment with the upstream XPUMD 2.0 Helm chart and image.
- https://sonda.red/notes/08-kleym-inference-identity/ - Building Kleym, a Kubernetes operator that maps inference resources to deterministic SPIFFE identity registration.
- https://sonda.red/notes/07-intel-homelab-5/ - Moving inference routing from Ingress toward Gateway API and agentgateway after llm-d made scheduling part of the routing problem.
- https://sonda.red/notes/06-intel-homelab-4/ - Adding llm-d to a Kubernetes inference stack so vLLM replicas can be routed with inference-aware scheduling.
- https://sonda.red/notes/05-intel-homelab-3/ - Building a Kubernetes inference MVP with Intel Arc GPUs, vLLM, DRA, ModelKits, OpenWebUI, and observability.
- https://sonda.red/notes/04-intel-homelab-2/ - Scaffolding the k3s cluster foundation for the Intel GPU homelab.
- https://sonda.red/notes/03-intel-homelab-1/ - Assembling the Intel-powered homelab hardware and explaining why the setup exists.
